questions.q: Sales of 100 vary by 10 and sales of 1000 vary by 100. Which transform is the first choice?
why: Correct: the spread is proportional to the level, so the log makes it constant.
Squaring makes the spread grow even faster.

Monthly sales have trend and a yearly season. What is a good order of steps?
options: Take the ordinary difference if a trend remains

questions.q: Your model predicts differences of log sales. The last log value is 5.0 and the forecast difference is +0.1. What is the forecast of sales (rounded)?
A teammate differences a series three times 'to be safe'. What is the risk?
options: Over-differencing adds negative autocorrelation and more noise
Nothing, more differencing is always better
why: Correct: extra differences add noise and a negative lag-1 correlation, so forecasts get worse.
Differencing makes a series more stationary, not less. The problem is added noise.
More is not better. It hurts the model.
